# mailcow_rspamd_setting (Resource)

Rule of Mailcow's Rspamd settings map (System → Configuration → Rspamd settings map). Mailcow passes `content` to Rspamd as the body of a settings rule without checking its syntax: a rule with a syntax error stops Rspamd from loading the whole settings map, Mailcow's own rules included. Check the rule on the server after applying, e.g. with `rspamc`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Don't count a Reply-To on another domain as spoofing for the site's own
# form notifications (they reply to the visitor) — and only for them.
resource "mailcow_rspamd_setting" "form_notifications" {
  description = "example.com form notifications: allow visitor Reply-To"
  content     = <<-EOT
    priority = high;
    rcpt = "hello@example.com";
    header = {
      "From" = "/noreply@example\.com/i";
    }
    apply {
      symbols_disabled = ["SPOOF_REPLYTO"];
    }
  EOT
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `content` (String) Body of the Rspamd settings rule, e.g. `priority`, conditions (`rcpt`, `from`, `header`…) and `apply { … }`. Compared with line endings and surrounding whitespace normalized.
- `description` (String) Short description shown in the Mailcow admin. Required: Mailcow's edit endpoint keeps the stored value when it receives an empty one.

### Optional

- `active` (Boolean) Whether Rspamd applies the rule

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The import id is the rule's numeric id ("ID #n" in the Mailcow admin)
terraform import mailcow_rspamd_setting.form_notifications 1
```
